title: renderToString and why it can't stream

slides.text: The oldest server API has a catch ⚠️
slides.say: Render to string is the simplest way to turn React into HTML. But it has a big limit.
You pass it your app, and it gives back an HTML string right away.

slides.text: It returns immediately, so it can't stream and can't wait for data. If a component suspends, the HTML gets the nearest Suspense fallback.
slides.say: Because it returns at once, it can't stream and it can't wait for data. If a component suspends, render to string puts the closest Suspense fallback in the HTML instead.

slides.code:
<Suspense fallback={<Spinner />}>
  <Posts /> {/* suspends */}
</Suspense>

// renderToString HTML:
// only the <Spinner />
// Posts appear after the client loads
slides.say: So here the HTML only contains the spinner. The posts don't show up until the client code loads.

slides.text: Prefer renderToPipeableStream on Node.js, or renderToReadableStream with Web Streams. Keep renderToString only where streams aren't supported.
slides.say: On Node, prefer render to pipeable stream. With web streams, use render to readable stream. Keep render to string only if your server can't use streams.
